tagline: Back roads through the farm district that turned away a prison.
intro: From US 250 near Zion Crossroads, Route 613 goes by four names, Poindexter, Oakland, Goldmine and Mansfield roads, on its way to US 522 at Wares Crossroads. On the way it marks part of the edge of Green Springs, 14,000 acres of manor houses and farms on a heavy clay that holds moisture, where the country around is poor soil and scrub pine.

In the early 1970s the state planned a detention center here. Owners put more than 7,000 acres under easement in a few months, opponents went to court, and Green Springs became the first rural National Historic Landmark district.

moments.title: Poindexter
moments.text: Probably named for the postman who ran its post office and store in the 1850s. Both are gone. Foster Creek Baptist Church, built in 1795 as Siloam, is not.

moments.title: Trevilian Station
moments.text: In June 1864 Sheridan and Hampton fought the war's largest all-cavalry battle here, and Custer, having captured Hampton's supply train, soon found himself surrounded.
